title: WPSS/526/2011 of MOHAN HARI PATHAK Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 526 of 2011
Mohan Hari Pathak Ö Petitioner
Vs
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
Mr. S.S. Yadav, Advocate, present for the petitioner.
Mr. Vikas Pande, Brief Holder, present for the State of Uttarakhand.
Honíble Manoj K. Tiwari, J. (Oral)
1. Heard Mr. S.S. Yadav, learned counsel for the
petitioner, Mr. Vikas Pande, Brief Holder for the State and
perused the records.
2. Petitioner participated in a selection for the post of
Instructor (Fitter) pursuant to an advertisement issued by
Director, Training and Employment, Uttarakhand on
20.06.2010. Upon completion of selection, result of all other
successful candidates was declared on 27.08.2010. However,
petitionerís result has not been declared so far on the ground
that teaching experience, which he possessed, is from
Industrial Training Institutes (in short ìITIî) situated in State of
Uttar Pradesh. It is the grievance of the petitioner that he has
been wrongly denied the bonus marks admissible for teaching
experience, which resulted in denial of appointment to him.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that as
per advertisement, a candidate having experience of teaching in
Government ITI will be entitled to one bonus mark for each
completed year of service. Learned counsel for the petitioner
submits that since petitioner has teaching experience of six
years from Government ITI, Bareilly, therefore, he is entitled for
six bonus marks in terms of the advertisement. He further
submits that petitioner scored 63.50 marks in written
examination and if six marks for experience are added, then
petitionerís score would be 69.50. Learned counsel further
submits that the last selected candidate for the post of
Instructor (Fitter) belonging to General category scored only
64.75 marks, which indicates that petitioner has been wrongly

2
denied appointment. Mr. Yadav, therefore, submits that
direction be issued to the Competent Authority to add six
bonus marks in petitionerís score of written examination and
issue appropriate order accordingly.
4. Mr. Vikas Pande, learned Brief Holder for the State,
on the other hand, submits that as per the advertisement,
bonus marks were to be given only to those candidates who
have acquired experience while serving in Government ITI in
Uttarakhand. According to him, since petitioner acquired such
experience while serving in Government ITI in State of Uttar
Pradesh, therefore, he is not entitled to any bonus marks. He
further submits that no other candidate, who acquired
experience from Government ITI situtate outside Uttarakhand,
was given benefit of bonus marks, therefore, the grievance of
the petitioner is without any substance.
5. Mr. S.S. Yadav, learned counsel for the petitioner
submits that there are still many vacancies available on the
post of Instructor (Fitter) in the department, therefore,
petitioner can easily be appointed against one of those
vacancies.
6. Mr. Vikas Pande, Brief Holder for the State disputes
this statement and submits that Director, Training and
Employment, has issued a public notice on 26.07.2016
whereby all concerned were informed that selection process
initiated in the year 2010 has come to an end.
7. Mr. S.S. Yadav, learned counsel for the petitioner
submits in reply that the instant writ petition is pending since
07.06.2011, therefore, right of the petitioner cannot be
extinguished by any public notice issued by the department
during pendency of the writ petition.

3
8. After considering the rival submissions of the
parties, I am of the opinion that experience acquired by a
candidate, while serving in Government ITI outside the State of
Uttarakhand, cannot be ignored. Moreover, in the
advertisement there is nothing to indicate that experience has
to be acquired only from Government ITI within Uttarakhand
State. The respondents cannot take benefit of ambiguity in the
advertisement.
9. In the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, I
am of the opinion that interest of justice would be served, if the
Director, Training & Employment is directed to examine the
matter and pass appropriate orders, in accordance with law.
10. Accordingly, the writ petition is disposed of with a
direction to Director, Training & Employment, Uttarakhand to
examine petitionerís claim for appointment, as Instructor
(Fitter) and pass a reasoned and speaking order, within six
weeks from the date of presentation of certified copy of this
order.
(Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
02.08.2017
Aswal
